items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this for a premium documentary YouTube Shorts channel about money, history and the tricks behind them. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller with a hint of mystery: curious, quietly amused, energetic and punchy, never slow, never announcer-like. Natural emphasis on dates and numbers, questions end with a curious lift, a short comic pause before each punchline. Keep the same voice, pace and energy from start to finish. Chars voices two funny cartoon characters (a smug gold bar and a nervous banknote), short and punchy, performed exactly as described in each bracket.
lines: Narrator
Your phone rings. Police say you're under arrest. Would you pay two hundred and sixty thousand dollars to make it stop?
Narrator
One woman in India did, in a single week.
Narrator
There's no such thing as a "digital arrest." The officer was a scammer.
Chars
[nervous, squeaky banknote, trembling, honest] I'd have paid too.
Narrator
So why do smart people pay?
Narrator
A parcel in your name. Drugs inside. A uniform, a fake police station.
Narrator
Then: don't hang up, and tell no one.
Narrator
In twenty twenty-four, Indians lost over two hundred million dollars this way.
Narrator
And then comes the part that empties accounts.
Narrator
To clear your name, you move your savings to a "safe" account.
Narrator
That's the mirage: the arrest feels real because you never stop watching.
Narrator
Now India's Supreme Court says banks that miss red flags should pay victims back.
Narrator
Real police never arrest you on a video call. Or ask for money.
Narrator
Comment: would you have hung up?
Narrator
This is Money Mirage. Follow for more.
